instruction: My work meeting files are available in the "~/documents/work/meetings_data/" directory in my file system. Currently, they are organized as "<date>__<file_name>.<extension>". Reorganize them in this format, "<file_name>/<date>.<extension>".
notes: Single-app task (file_system). The agent must list ~/documents/work/meetings_data/, then for every file '<date>__<file_name>.<ext>' create the subdirectory '<file_name>/' (once per distinct file_name) and move the file to '<file_name>/<date>.<ext>' via move_file, which preserves content (evaluation requires identical content at the new paths and all other files untouched). The exact number of files is only known at runtime, so the problem uses three placeholder file objects (two sharing one <file_name> subdirectory, one in another) to illustrate directory reuse; at runtime repeat the move (and one create_directory per distinct file_name) for each listed file. Knowledge of the files/paths is modeled by the nullary (meeting-files-listed) asserted by show_directory on the meetings directory; static facts map each file to its source path, destination path and destination directory. create_directory must precede the moves into that directory. supervisor-complete-task takes the meeting-file records as non-API parameters (with inequality constraints) so that its precondition is exactly the goal conjunction; it is the only action that asserts (task-completed) and every other action requires (not (task-completed)), so it is necessarily last. Apps are declared as domain constants (file-system) and are not redeclared as problem objects.
